knowledge:
- key_parameters: ctc=Prior distribution parameters (Beta) for circulating tumor cells inter-mixed with white blood cells in the buffy coat (e.g., list(a=1, b=10e3)) ;; ctdna=Prior distribution parameters (Beta) for ctDNA in plasma (e.g., list(a=1, b=9)) ;; chip=Prior distribution parameters (Beta) for germline or CHIP variants in WBCs (e.g., list(a=1, b=9)) ;; montecarlo.samples=Number of Monte Carlo simulations to run (e.g., 50e3) ;; prior.weight=Mixture weight for the prior in the importance sampler (e.g., 0.1 to concentrate mass on the posterior, or 1.0 to sample directly from the prior) ;; save_montecarlo=Logical flag in importance_sampler(); set to FALSE to save only marginal likelihoods and Bayes factors to conserve memory on large datasets
- alternatives: Rule-based analyses (e.g., filtering out mutations based on their presence/absence in buffy coat), which fail to account for uneven sequencing depths or circulating tumor cell contamination
- when_to_use: When analyzing liquid biopsy (cfDNA) mutation data alongside matched white blood cell (buffy coat) sequencing data to distinguish tumor-derived somatic mutations from clonal hematopoiesis (CH) mutations
- pitfalls: Using too few Monte Carlo samples when prior.weight = 1 (sampling from prior) leads to highly unstable Bayes factor estimates; importance sampling (prior.weight = 0.1) is highly recommended to maintain stability. Input data must be formatted as a nested tibble grouped by a unique mutation/sample identifier (uid) as required by importance_sampler.

workflows.name: plasmut_origin_quantification
workflows.intent: Quantify the likelihood of plasma mutations originating from tumor vs. clonal hematopoiesis using matched plasma and buffy coat sequencing data.
input: user_mutation_data.csv (containing columns for sample/patient ID, gene/mutation, analyte type ["plasma" or "buffy coat"], mutant read count [y], and total read count [n])
workflows.stages: 1. Format the input mutation data into a nested tibble grouped by a unique mutation identifier (uid) ;; 2. Define the prior parameters and Monte Carlo settings in a parameter list ;; 3. Run the importance sampler using importance_sampler() to calculate marginal likelihoods and Bayes factors ;; 4. Extract and interpret the log Bayes factors
workflows.code:
data(crcseq, package="plasmut")
params <- list(ctdna = list(a = 1, b = 9), 
               ctc = list(a = 1, b = 10^3), 
               chip = list(a= 1, b = 9), 
               montecarlo.samples = 50e3, 
               prior.weight = 0.1)
muts <- unite(crcseq, "uid", c(patient, gene), remove = FALSE) %>% 
        group_by(uid) %>% nest()
muts$IS <- muts$data %>% map(importance_sampler, params)
fun <- function(x){
    result <- x$data %>%
        select(-position) %>%
        mutate(bayes_factor = x$IS$bayesfactor$bayesfactor)
    return(result)
}
bf <- apply(muts, 1, fun) 
bf %>% do.call(rbind, .) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(patient, gene, aa, bayes_factor) %>%
    rename(log_bf=bayes_factor) %>%
    distinct()
